Air is the most important requirement for life on 
our planet. Each person requires an average of 20 Kg of air /day, which is about 
15 times more than the same person's daily food requirements. The quality of air 
is therefore a major health concern. Air pollution can be caused by either 
gaseous or particulate pollutants or both.

Emitted flue gases more than the permissible value, according to the law of 
environment 4 year 1994, are not allowed. Therefore the environmental 
administration in Talkha Power Station makes a scientific program in order to 
avoid and protect all the worked people in the station from the hazards.

 conductor inside or outside the instrument or disconnection of the protective 
 earth terminal is likely to make the apparatus dangerous. Intentional

When the apparatus is connected its 
 supply, terminals may be live, and the opening of covers of removal of parts (

Any adjustment, maintenance and 
 repair of the opened apparatus under voltage shall be avoided as far as

Make sure that only fuses with the

Whenever it is likely that the

Shows visible damage.

Fails to perform the intended

Has been subjected to prolonged

Has been subjected to severe

sections.text:
Due caution should be exercised 
 when installing, operation and servicing this equipment. Attention is drawn to 
 the following safety points:

Ensure that main supplies are 
 isolated, when making access to the equipment for maintenance or servicing 
 purposes. Read the instructions carefully to ensure correction of all mains, 
 signal leads and probe connections.

Eyes and face should be suitable 
 protected by goggles when looking into hot furnaces. Precaution should also be 
 taken when removing instruments from pressurized ducts.

When working in the vicinity of hot 
 boilers and furnaces, protective clothing should be worn at all times, 
 particularly protection of the hands.

The instrument must be fully 
 isolated from the power supply before internal, electrical maintenance or 
 servicing work, and should only be undertaken by a suitable authorized/ 
 qualified engineer.

Under certain boiler conditions a 
 high static charge may build up. With non conductive stack entry points the 
 normal procedure to avoid damage to the instrument or person, is to make a 
 connection from the probe extension to ground /earth before inserting into 
 stack. With conductive (metallic) entry points the metal surround should be 
 grounded.

Situations may occur, for instance 
 where the sampled hot gases have just passed through electrostatic 
 precipitators, where a high static charge would build up on the instrument 
 probe if ungrounded. Further contact by any grounded object, i.e. a person 
 touching the keyboard and forming a discharge path, may then result in damage 
 to the instrument.

All recognized safety procedures 
 should be used when operating with hazardous gases.

Land Combustion accepts no 
 responsibility for damage to the instrument, or injury to the person while 
 following procedures, nor will the company accepts liability for failure to 
 comply with safety precautions.

Note: A special 
heated smoke probe must be used to perform any smoke measurements.

Select 
the SMOKE option from the main menu. Follow on screen instructions.

The heated smoke probe is fitted in 
place of the gas probe. The smoke probe connects using the same input ports as 
the standard gas probe. Allow approximately 1 
minute for the probe to heat up.

Insert filter paper in the holder 
inside the probe handle mechanism. Once ready insert the probe into the flue gas stream.

The 
elapse time necessary for the probe to make an accurate measurement can be set 
in the SETUP SYSTEM menu. It is possible to adjust both the elapse time 
(default time 30 sec. and the pump speed default 7500 to either increase or 
decrease the quantity of smoke deposited on the filter. A flow meter (not 
supplied) is necessary to determine flow rate of the flue gas, to calculate the 
elapse time to make an accurate reading. 
Note: Regulations 
govern the exact conditions of acceptable smoke measurement. This is dependent 
upon the country and the regulatory body. Check for local regulations to ensure 
the measurement meets the accepted standard.

The 
elapse time will count down until sufficient smoke as passed the filter to make 
an acceptable measurement.

Remove 
the smoke filter paper from pistol grip handle.

The 
grayness of the paper has to be compared against a standard Bacharach chart to 
give an indication of density.

Safety Precautions
Before switching on the apparatus 
 make sure that the power supply is suitable for the instrument.
The mains/power plug shall only be 
 inserted in a socket outlet provided with a protective earth contact. The 
 protective action must not be negated by the use of an extension card without 
 a protective conductor.
Warning
Any interruption of the protective 
 conductor inside or outside the instrument or disconnection of the protective 
 earth terminal is likely to make the apparatus dangerous. Intentional 
 interruption is prohibited.
When the apparatus is connected its 
 supply, terminals may be live, and the opening of covers of removal of parts ( 
 except those to which access can be gained by hand ) is likely to expose live 
 parts.
Any adjustment, maintenance and 
 repair of the opened apparatus under voltage shall be avoided as far as 
 possible and, if inevitable, shall be carried out only by a shelled person who 
 is aware of the hazard involved.
Make sure that only fuses with the 
 required rated current and of the specified type are used for replacement.
The use of makeshift fused and the 
 short circuiting of fuse holders are prohibited.
Whenever it is likely that the 
 protection has been impaired, the apparatus shall be made inoperative and be 
 secured against any an intended operation.
The protection is likely to be 
 impaired if, for example, the apparatus:
Shows visible damage.
Fails to perform the intended 
 measurements.
Has been subjected to prolonged 
 storage under unfavorable conditions .
Has been subjected to severe 
 transport stresses.
Safety Aspects Continued
Caution
Due caution should be exercised 
 when installing, operation and servicing this equipment. Attention is drawn to 
 the following safety points:
Power
Ensure that main supplies are 
 isolated, when making access to the equipment for maintenance or servicing 
 purposes. Read the instructions carefully to ensure correction of all mains, 
 signal leads and probe connections.
Eye Protection
Eyes and face should be suitable 
 protected by goggles when looking into hot furnaces. Precaution should also be 
 taken when removing instruments from pressurized ducts.
Protective Clothing
When working in the vicinity of hot 
 boilers and furnaces, protective clothing should be worn at all times, 
 particularly protection of the hands.
Fault Finding
The instrument must be fully 
 isolated from the power supply before internal, electrical maintenance or 
 servicing work, and should only be undertaken by a suitable authorized/ 
 qualified engineer.
Static Discharge
Under certain boiler conditions a 
 high static charge may build up. With non conductive stack entry points the 
 normal procedure to avoid damage to the instrument or person, is to make a 
 connection from the probe extension to ground /earth before inserting into 
 stack. With conductive (metallic) entry points the metal surround should be 
 grounded.
Situations may occur, for instance 
 where the sampled hot gases have just passed through electrostatic 
 precipitators, where a high static charge would build up on the instrument 
 probe if ungrounded. Further contact by any grounded object, i.e. a person 
 touching the keyboard and forming a discharge path, may then result in damage 
 to the instrument.
Hazardous Gases
All recognized safety procedures 
 should be used when operating with hazardous gases.
Land Combustion accepts no 
 responsibility for damage to the instrument, or injury to the person while 
 following procedures, nor will the company accepts liability for failure to 
 comply with safety precautions.

Smoke Measurements
Note: A special 
heated smoke probe must be used to perform any smoke measurements.
Select 
the SMOKE option from the main menu. Follow on screen instructions.
The heated smoke probe is fitted in 
place of the gas probe. The smoke probe connects using the same input ports as 
the standard gas probe. Allow approximately 1 
minute for the probe to heat up.
Insert filter paper in the holder 
inside the probe handle mechanism. Once ready insert the probe into the flue gas stream.
Press 
GO (F4) on the instrument.
The 
elapse time necessary for the probe to make an accurate measurement can be set 
in the SETUP SYSTEM menu. It is possible to adjust both the elapse time 
(default time 30 sec. and the pump speed default 7500 to either increase or 
decrease the quantity of smoke deposited on the filter. A flow meter (not 
supplied) is necessary to determine flow rate of the flue gas, to calculate the 
elapse time to make an accurate reading. 
Note: Regulations 
govern the exact conditions of acceptable smoke measurement. This is dependent 
upon the country and the regulatory body. Check for local regulations to ensure 
the measurement meets the accepted standard.
The 
elapse time will count down until sufficient smoke as passed the filter to make 
an acceptable measurement.
Remove 
the smoke filter paper from pistol grip handle.
The 
grayness of the paper has to be compared against a standard Bacharach chart to 
give an indication of density.
